Experimental: first sign in multiple accounts for the same drive on the drive page; only then do the switches below take effect.

Multi-account download: when downloading in bulk, each file rotates through different accounts to fetch links, bypassing a single account\'s concurrency / speed limits (each file still uses only one account to download).

Multi-source chunking for a single file: the same file fetches one direct link per account, and chunks are handed to different direct links in turn, genuinely speeding up a single large file; currently only effective on Quark / UC / Xunlei / Baidu, other platforms still download single-source.

Both features make multiple accounts hit the same drive within a short time, making risk control more likely than usual; if you hit a captcha, rate limiting, or slower downloads, just turn the switches off to recover.

Please sign in only to your own accounts. Frequently rotating multiple accounts to fetch links on the same network may trigger risk control on some drives (especially Baidu and Quark): captchas, temporary rate limiting, or even short-term download restrictions on the account. This feature is still experimental; you can turn it off anytime if something goes wrong.
Enable \"Multi-source chunking for a single file\"?

The same file will be fetched by multiple accounts at once, which is more likely to trigger risk control than multi-account download; you may see a higher chunk failure rate, slower downloads, or a temporarily restricted account. Currently only Quark / UC / Xunlei / Baidu are supported. This feature is still experimental; please assess the risk yourself.
